title: Jadę autobusem
note: Third job of the instrumental: identity (Jestem nauczycielem) → company (z bratem) → means (autobusem). Same case, same -em every time; that callback is the unit's gift and it opens intro slide 2. The single teaching point is the ABSENCE of a preposition — English 'by bus' has two words, Polish has none — so *z autobusem is planted as a wrong choice in nine of the twelve quiz items and the five Pisanie sentence items exist purely so the learner has a slot in front of the noun that he must leave empty. Seven forms only: autobusem, tramwajem, samochodem, rowerem, pociągiem (g pulls in i, the a1_gen_ki fact doing a third job, same as z wujkiem), plus neuter metrem and autem, which take the same -em he met in dzieckiem. Forks taken, conservative path per batch rule 7: (a) taksi IS in POOL and is genuinely indeclinable, but it is shown once in an intro table as a curiosity and never drilled, never demanded by a prompt — a whole stage of 'type nothing' would teach nothing, and the learner's job here is the ending; (b) karetka was considered as a feminine -ą form and rejected — 'by ambulance' is not everyday language for this learner and a lone feminine would dilute the one ending the unit is built on; (c) samochód → samochodem carries an ó→o stem shift, which a2_gen_pl fenced. It is unavoidable (samochód is the everyday word for car and the brief names it) so it is taught whole, flagged on its own intro row and given an explain in quiz and Pisanie; auto/autem sits beside it as the shift-free alternative. (d) jechać is assumed to supply exactly six present forms (jadę/jedziesz/jedzie/jedziemy/jedziecie/jadą) from a2_jechac and nothing else — no past of jechać anywhere, no prefixed motion verbs. FENCED: plural instrumental (autobusami), pieszo / na piechotę, past of jechać, prefixed motion verbs (pojechać, przyjechać), na rowerze / w autobusie (locative rivals, untaught), and czym — the question word is never used, hence the title Jadę autobusem.

intro.title: Polish has no word for by
intro.body:
English needs two words: by + bus.

Polish needs none. The ending on the vehicle does the whole job.

Jadę autobusem. = I'm going by bus.

Look at what is not there. No z, no other little word — nothing at all stands in front of autobusem. The ending -em is the whole of by.

This is the one thing to get right in this unit. English will push you to write z autobusem, and that is wrong. z is for the person you travel with, never for the vehicle.
intro.body_pl: Środek transportu: sam narzędnik, bez przyimka.

intro.title: One case, three jobs
intro.body:
This is the instrumental (narzędnik) for the third time. You have now used one case for three different duties, and the endings have never changed.

That is the whole trick of Polish cases: you learn the endings once and they keep paying out. Masculine takes -em — in nauczycielem, in z bratem, and now in autobusem.
intro.body_pl: Ten sam przypadek, trzecie zadanie. Końcówka bez zmian: -em.

rows: I'm going to the park with my brother.

intro.title: The forms
intro.body:
Seven vehicles, one ending. Add -em to the vehicle and you have said by.

metro and auto are neuter, and neuter takes -em too — the ending you already met in On jest dzieckiem.
intro.body_pl: m. -em, n. -em. Ta sama końcówka co w dzieckiem.

intro.title: Two to watch, one that never moves
intro.body:
pociąg → pociągiem. Polish does not put a plain e straight after g here; the g pulls an i in front of the ending, giving -iem. You have seen this fact twice already — in banki and książki, and in z wujkiem. After k and g, Polish reaches for i.

samochód → samochodem. The ó flattens to a plain o the moment an ending is added. Learn the finished word whole.

taksi never changes at all. Jadę taksi. It is one of a small handful of borrowed words that take no endings ever — a gift, not a rule.
intro.body_pl: g → -iem (jak wujkiem). ó → o. taksi nieodmienne.

examples.en: My brother is going to work by car.
We're going to the city by tram.
Dad is going by car with mum.
The children are going to school by bus.

quiz.explain: English by has no Polish word in front of it here. z belongs to people you travel with — z bratem — and never to the vehicle. The ending -em is doing all the work.
The g will not sit straight in front of a plain e, so it pulls an i in first: -iem. Exactly what happened in z wujkiem, and the same fact as banki and książki.
The ó only survives when nothing follows it. Add an ending and it flattens to a plain o: samochód, but samochodem.
metro is neuter, and neuter takes the same -em as masculine. You met it once before in On jest dzieckiem.
People keep their z. Only vehicles go bare. That is the whole difference: z bratem, but autobusem.

quiz.prompt: My brother is going to work by bus. →
choices: Brat jedzie do pracy z autobusem.

quiz.prompt: Dad is going by car with mum. →
choices: Tata jedzie z samochodem z mamą.
quiz.explain: One case doing two of its jobs in one sentence. Both nouns are in the instrumental; only the person gets a z in front of it.

quiz.prompt: We're going to the city by train. →

quiz.explain: A question changes nothing inside the sentence. czy opens it, and the vehicle keeps its bare -em ending.

type_items.explain: No ó in the middle. The vowel flattens to o as soon as an ending arrives.
Four letters at the end, not three: g asks for an i before the ending, so it is -giem.
Two words and no more. Nothing goes in front of autobusem — the space where English puts by stays empty in Polish.

use_items.prompt_en: Type: My brother is going to work by bus.
accepts: Mój brat jedzie do pracy autobusem.
Mój brat jedzie do pracy autobusem
use_items.explain: Two nouns, two different cases: do pracy is the genitive (where to), autobusem the instrumental (how). Only one of them takes a preposition.

use_items.prompt_en: Type: Mum is going to the shop by car. (samochód)
Type: Dad is going to the city by train.
Type: My son is going to school by bike.
accepts: Mój syn jedzie do szkoły rowerem.
Mój syn jedzie do szkoły rowerem

use_items.prompt_en: Type: My sister is going to the centre by metro.
accepts: Moja siostra jedzie do centrum metrem.
Moja siostra jedzie do centrum metrem

use_items.prompt_en: Type: Grandad is going to the pharmacy by tram.
Type: Mum is going to the office by bus with dad.
use_items.answer: Mama jedzie do biura autobusem z tatą.
accepts: Mama jedzie do biura autobusem z tatą.
Mama jedzie do biura autobusem z tatą
use_items.explain: The same case twice over: autobusem is how she travels, z tatą is who with. The person needs z, the bus does not.

use_items.prompt_en: Type: Is dad going to work by car? (samochód)
use_items.answer: Czy tata jedzie do pracy samochodem?
accepts: Czy tata jedzie do pracy samochodem?
Czy tata jedzie do pracy samochodem

use_items.prompt_en: Type: The children are going to school by bus.
use_items.explain: dzieci is plural, so the verb is jadą — but the vehicle is untouched by that. autobusem stays exactly as it was.

use_items.prompt_en: Type: My friend is going home by train. (kolega)
Type: Grandma is going to the hotel by car. (auto)
Type: My granddaughter is going to the park by bike.
